title: Concise mentor guide for SDKs: first 3 commits
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact mentor-facing guide to help an experienced Redwood engineer shepherd a new SDK contributor through the first three commits that make an SDK repo shipping-ready for a minimal demo. The goal is high signal, low ceremony: by the end of three git commits the contributor should have a working sample that can be run locally, basic telemetry, and a CI smoke test.

Why this exists (context):
- Drive less friction for new contributors and partner teams building SDKs.
- Reduce review cycles by standardizing what a minimal acceptable initial PR contains.
- Increase confidence that early commits include necessary safety, telemetry, and docs so later work can iterate on features.

Audience: mentor engineers, SDK maintainers, new SDK contributors (internal).

Assumptions:
- Repo created from sdk-template (internal) or forked.
- Language conventions follow existing Redwood SDK patterns (auth via env var, simple client class, README skeleton).
- Local dev machine has Docker, Python/Node runtime, and the Redwood CLI dev shim installed.

Quick overview (the three commits):
1) commit-1: "initial-sample-and-readme" — add a minimal sample app + README with run steps
2) commit-2: "basic-telemetry-and-config" — wire minimal telemetry + config knobs + env validation
3) commit-3: "ci-smoke-test-and-lint" — add one CI job that runs sample smoke test and linter

Detailed checklist per commit (mentor should verify):

Commit 1: initial-sample-and-readme
- Files added: README.md, examples/quickstart.{py,js}, minimal client import usage.
- README includes: 3 lines to run (install, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run sample), expected output snippet, link to full docs.
- Sample respects timeouts and has clear input/output; avoid long generative prompts in sample (use short prompt).
- Local run uses a small model profile or mock endpoint so it runs in <30s for reviewer.
- Inline TODO markers for future expansion (e.g., "TODO: show streaming example").
- Commit message format: "initial-sample-and-readme: add minimal quickstart sample"

Mentor guidance for commit 1:
- Ask contributor to run the sample on their machine and paste the exact console output in the PR description. This reduces back-and-forth.
- Verify README run steps work on a clean environment (Docker is preferred).

Commit 2: basic-telemetry-and-config
- Add minimal telemetry events emitted by the client: startup, sample_invocation, error.
- Telemetry must be togglable via env var (REDWOOD_SDK_TELEMETRY=false).
- Telemetry payload: SDK name, version, language, run_id, success|failure, latency_ms (rounded). Keep payload small and non-sensitive.
- Add config validation: check REDWOOD_API_KEY presence and basic shape; surface friendlier error messages.
- Add a small docs section in README explaining telemetry and how to disable it.
- Commit message format: "basic-telemetry-and-config: add opt-out telemetry + env validation"

Mentor guidance for commit 2:
- Review telemetry payload for PII; mentor should insist no user text is sent. If sample uses user prompt, telemetry must only include prompt length not content.
- Point to Confluence telemetry spec (linked) if there is any ambiguity.

Commit 3: ci-smoke-test-and-lint
- Add CI workflow/job (github actions or internal runner) that:
  - Installs deps
  - Runs linter/formatter (fail on lint errors)
  - Runs a smoke test that executes the quickstart sample against a mocked endpoint or with REDWOOD_API_KEY set to a short-lived test token provided via secrets.
- Smoke test must be <90s total and assert expected output substring.
- Add simple test harness under tests/test_smoke_quickstart.{py,js} that programmatically calls the quickstart function and asserts status.
- Commit message format: "ci-smoke-test-and-lint: add workflow + quickstart smoke test"

Mentor guidance for commit 3:
- Confirm CI secrets are configured (ask infra if not).
- If internal runners are flaky, prefer mocking network calls to make CI deterministic.

Review checklist (applies across all commits):
- Security: no API keys or secrets committed. No example keys in text.
- Simplicity: prefer short files and clear names; reviewers should be able to find the quickstart in <10s.
- Observability: telemetry events are present and documented with opt-out.
- Tests: at least one deterministic smoke test in CI.
- Documentation: README has 3-step run instructions and a short explanation of telemetry and config.

PR description template (mentor can paste this into review request):
- What this PR does (one sentence)
- How I validated it locally (exact commands + console output)
- CI expectations (which job should pass)
- Areas I want help on (list)

Example one-sentence PR description: "Adds minimal quickstart sample, opt-out telemetry, and a CI smoke test so the SDK can show a runnable demo in <2 minutes."

Common mentor talking points (use these in code review comments):
- "Can you show the console output you saw when running the quickstart locally? Paste it in the PR body."
- "Telemetry: confirm no user content is transmitted; prefer length/metadata only."
- "If CI is flaky, prefer mocks for network interactions in smoke test."
- "Thanks — this is a great minimal demo. For follow-ups, consider adding streaming example and role-based auth example."

Nice-to-have follow-ups (not required for the three commits):
- small example of streaming responses with a progress bar
- example of using Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching hint)
- structured output example with JSON schema enforcement
- a tiny tutorial notebook for interactive exploration

Troubleshooting notes for mentors:
- If contributor can't run sample: verify Docker/docker-compose network, runtime versions, and Node/Python path.
- If telemetry doesn't appear in dev logs: check the local telemetry dev sink and that REDWOOD_SDK_TELEMETRY=true.
- If CI secrets missing: ping infra with JIRA ticket DEVX-927 (linked).

Low bar acceptance criteria (for merging the initial PR):
- Quickstart runs locally in <30s on dev machine or via Docker and printed expected output.
- README has 3 run steps and a small explanation of telemetry and how to disable.
- CI smoke test exists and runs deterministically under mock or test token.
- No secrets or PII in repo.

Appendix: Example minimal telemetry payload (do not include user text):
- {"sdk":"redwood-python","version":"0.1.0","lang":"python","event":"sample_invocation","latency_ms":"120","result":"success"}

(mentor note: payload should be small JSON; remove any raw prompt content. See Confluence spec linked above.)

Estimated review time for mentor: 15–30 minutes for the three commits combined if contributor follows template.

Open questions to resolve in a follow-up doc:
- Should we provide a small official test token for smoke tests that is rate-limited? (pros: deterministic CI; cons: token rotation overhead)
- Standard file names for quickstart example across languages to make cross-repo tooling easier.

If you use this guide, please add a short note in the PR: "used mentor-guide v0" so we can gather metrics on adoption.

-- end of guide --
